reconstructed_theorem_text: For every measurable space U and every complete real normed vector space H, let K:U->H be strongly measurable. Let B,C,L be supplied finite nonnegative real constants. Assume norm_H(K(u))<=B for every u in U. Let c:U times U->R be measurable, with 0<=c(z)<=C for every z in U times U, and assume norm_H(K(u)-K(v))<=L*c(u,v) for every u,v in U. For every probability measures mu,nu on U use these definitions: Define cost:U times U->nonnegative_extended_reals by cost(u,v)=ofReal(c(u,v)^2), where ofReal takes the nonnegative part. Define Q as the infimum, in the extended nonnegative real line, of the values integral_lower_{U times U} cost(z) dgamma(z) over every measure gamma on U times U satisfying gamma.map Prod.fst=mu and gamma.map Prod.snd=nu. Here integral_lower denotes the nonnegative extended Lebesgue integral. The two marginal equalities are exactly the coupling constraints; no minimizing coupling or selected coupling is part of the definition. Let W=Q^(1/2), the extended nonnegative square root. Write m_mu=integral_U K(u) dmu(u) and m_nu=integral_U K(v) dnu(v), the actual H-valued Bochner integrals. Then all the following conclusions hold: K is genuinely Bochner integrable under mu; K is genuinely Bochner integrable under nu; Q is not infinity; norm_H(m_mu-m_nu)<=L*W.toReal; and for every y in H, both norm_H(m_mu-y)<=B+norm_H(y) and norm_H(m_nu-y)<=B+norm_H(y). The integrability and finiteness statements are produced conclusions rather than hypotheses. Strong measurability and the bound B under probability laws give genuine feature integrability. The coupling marginal constraints with probability endpoints allow couplings and force every coupling to have mass one; bounded c makes finite transport costs available, hence the asserted finite Q. The statement makes no claim that the infimum is attained. Since Q is finite, W is finite and W.toReal is its ordinary nonnegative real value, equal to sqrt(Q.toReal). The extended-real toReal operation sends infinity to zero in general, so the separate finiteness conclusion is essential and is retained explicitly. No positivity of Q is assumed, and Q=0 is included. The cost is the literal square c^2 with no extra factor, not an asserted squared metric. U has no topology or metric structure in the statement, and no symmetry, triangle inequality, diagonal-zero, or separation property of c is assumed. H need not be an inner-product space or finite dimensional; its completeness is explicitly required. All vector means and final vector norms are actual Bochner integrals and the norm of H. The last pair of inequalities is uniform over all y:H, with y fixed only when evaluating each norm.
objects: Measurable space U; complete real normed vector space H; strongly measurable bounded feature K; nonnegative real constants B,C,L; actual measurable nonnegative bounded scalar cost c on U times U; probability laws mu,nu; squared extended-nonnegative cost; coupling-constrained transport infimum Q; its square root W; actual vector means m_mu,m_nu; and arbitrary y:H.
domains: U has a MeasurableSpace structure only. H has NormedAddCommGroup, NormedSpace R, and CompleteSpace structures, without an inner-product or finite-dimensionality requirement. K:U->H is globally strongly measurable. B,C,L:R are finite and nonnegative. c:U times U->R is measurable for the product measurable structure. mu,nu:Measure U are probability measures. Couplings gamma:Measure(U times U) have the specified two pushforward marginals. cost,Q,W take values in the nonnegative extended reals; W.toReal and all inequality coefficients are real. The two means are H-valued Bochner integrals over all U, and y ranges over H.
quantifiers: For every U,H with the displayed structures, every K and its strong-measurability proof, every nonnegative B,C,L satisfying the pointwise feature bound, every measurable c satisfying both pointwise cost bounds and the comparison norm(K(u)-K(v))<=L*c(u,v) for every u,v, and every probability mu,nu, define cost,Q,W. All conjunction clauses then hold. Inside Q the infimum ranges over the cost values of every coupling with the exact two marginal equalities. The last outer clause universally quantifies every y:H and asserts both mean-to-y inequalities. No existential optimizer or estimate constant is quantified.
assumptions: The given complete real normed-space structure on H and measurable-space structure on U; strong measurability of K; B,C,L>=0; pointwise norm(K(u))<=B; measurability of c; pointwise 0<=c(z)<=C; pointwise norm(K(u)-K(v))<=L*c(u,v); and mu,nu both probability measures. No prior Bochner integrability under these endpoint laws, finite transport-cost premise, chosen coupling, optimal-coupling assumption, metric axioms, or positivity of Q is supplied.
conclusion: K is genuinely Bochner integrable under mu; K is genuinely Bochner integrable under nu; Q is not infinity; norm_H(m_mu-m_nu)<=L*W.toReal; and for every y in H, both norm_H(m_mu-y)<=B+norm_H(y) and norm_H(m_nu-y)<=B+norm_H(y). Define Q as the infimum, in the extended nonnegative real line, of the values integral_lower_{U times U} cost(z) dgamma(z) over every measure gamma on U times U satisfying gamma.map Prod.fst=mu and gamma.map Prod.snd=nu. Here integral_lower denotes the nonnegative extended Lebesgue integral. The two marginal equalities are exactly the coupling constraints; no minimizing coupling or selected coupling is part of the definition. Let W=Q^(1/2), the extended nonnegative square root. Write m_mu=integral_U K(u) dmu(u) and m_nu=integral_U K(v) dnu(v), the actual H-valued Bochner integrals.
scopes: The feature integrability is genuine, so both H-valued means are actual finite Bochner integrals rather than totalized values of nonintegrable functions. The transport cost is an extended-nonnegative infimum of nonnegative extended integrals, with mu as first and nu as second marginal, over arbitrary coupling measures satisfying those equalities. c need not be symmetric, so the ordering of the marginals is preserved. The explicit finiteness conjunct is Q!=infinity; it also makes W finite, ensuring W.toReal represents the finite square root rather than the special toReal value at infinity. The norm comparison uses exactly L times that finite real value. The cost remains ofReal(c(z)^2), with no signed integral, metric interpretation, or optimizer implicit. The final inequalities apply to every vector y and use the same B for both endpoints. Zero values of B,C,L or Q are allowed subject to the stated hypotheses. All norm comparisons are in H, not a hidden Hilbert space.
constant_dependencies: B controls the pointwise feature norm, yields integrability under probability laws, and appears exactly as B+norm(y) in both final bounds. C is the supplied pointwise bound on c and supplies finite transport costs; it does not appear as an extra multiplicative factor in the stated mean-displacement inequality. L is exactly the coefficient in the feature-cost comparison and in norm(m_mu-m_nu)<=L*W.toReal. The transport construction uses c squared and exponent 1/2 with no extra factor or normalization. The coupling laws have mass one from their probability marginals. No unspecified universal constant, dimension factor, or optimality claim appears.
